LESSON: VISUAL PROGRAMMING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.4: Visual Programming

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Visual Programming. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are computer programs used in day-to-day life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify types of visual programming applications used in day-to-day life
2. create instructions to solve problems using visual programming application
3. value the importance of visual programming in day- to-day life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: VISUAL PROGRAMMING
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Visual Programming helps you succeed in PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

KEY FACTS: VISUAL PROGRAMMING
Study Visual Programming like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify types of visual programming applications used in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to identify types of visual programming applications used in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify types of visual programming applications used in day-to-day life.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Safety first: State one safety rule before practising “Visual Programming”.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify types of visual programming applications used in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create instructions to solve problems using visual programming application

What this means
In this part you learn to create instructions to solve problems using visual programming application. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create instructions to solve problems using visual programming application.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Steps: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Visual Programming.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create instructions to solve problems using visual programming application. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value the importance of visual programming in day- to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to value the importance of visual programming in day- to-day life. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the importance of visual programming in day- to-day life.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Check: Inspect your work and say one improvement.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the importance of visual programming in day- to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Visual Programming is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: State one safety rule before practising “Visual Programming”. (skill: identify types of visual programming applications used in day-to-day life)

Example 2: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Visual Programming. (skill: create instructions to solve problems using visual programming application)

Example 3: Inspect your work and say one improvement. (skill: value the importance of visual programming in day- to-day life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Visual Programming to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify types of visual programming applications used in day-to-day life.
3. Practise this skill: create instructions to solve problems using visual programming application.
4. Practise this skill: value the importance of visual programming in day- to-day life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Visual Programming from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Visual Programming: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Visual Programming?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are computer programs used in day-to-day life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Visual Programming means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify types of visual programming applications used in day-to-day life.
5. Be able to: create instructions to solve problems using visual programming application.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
